quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop like you would on other roads. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic on the interstate, then merge smoothly when safe.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before the turn.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, unless a sign says no. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to enter your lane without warning.
Assume other drivers and pedestrians will respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to enter your lane without warning.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. People may step out without looking. Parked vehicles may start moving suddenly.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive onto the shoulder or off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual spot, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle is visible to all approaching drivers so it does not become a hazard.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a deadly crash.
Higher speeds mean you need a greater following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 mph, survival is unlikely. Higher speeds also require longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance as you go faster.

questions.question: Your car starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front of your car in line with the rear and straightens your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They disappear if you have one mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: Water on the road causes hydroplaning. This can happen at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: What does an orange sign like this mean?

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark construction areas. Drive carefully through these areas.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check that no vehicles are in your way. Always look behind and to the side of your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
Are not affected by vehicle speed.
Increase as vehicle speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as vehicle speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Right turn on red light is permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line over a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Bad weather makes it hard for other drivers to see your vehicle. Headlights make your car easier to see. If you need windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Won't affect your driving.
Won't put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed carefully.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When these lines are next to each other, you can only pass from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.question: If your car has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part gives you much less protection. If your car has an automatic shoulder belt, still buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: The right way to turn right is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right edge before turning.
Stay near the right edge, then move toward the center before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right edge before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay in the right lane, as close to the right edge as possible.

questions.question: If your car loses grip on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the same speed to get better grip.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down slowly and do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down slowly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road on water, it is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes.

questions.question: Construction zone signs usually look like:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you. What do you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles with lights and sirens go first. Move to the right edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: To make room for cars entering the freeway:

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Make space for cars entering the freeway. If you can, move to another lane to create a gap. If you cannot move, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabilities. Only cars with disability license plates or disability placards can park here.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are moving. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are not sure about an oncoming car's speed, wait until it passes and you can see clearly before you pass.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the nearest rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks do not replace real rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means two things. It tells you the protected left turn is ending. It also means you must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your car wheels go off the edge of the road. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your car leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly and release the gas pedal. Gently apply the brakes. Slow down before looking for a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or cross into other lanes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Another car is passing you in a no passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down so the other car can safely return to the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other car can safely return to the lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely for better traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to low gear before going down steep hills on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you don't have antilock brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Upcoming change in direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you are going to do.
